title: Testing Sign Agreement
abstract: arXiv:2608.10294v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This article studies the problem of testing sign agreement among a finite number of parameters, with applications to dynamic treatment effects, instrument validity, and labor-market discrimination. We propose least favorable and two-step tests that accommodate correlated estimators. Both have parametric and nonparametric bootstrap implementations and uniform asymptotic validity. Although neither test dominates the other in general, local power analysis shows that the two-step test can gain power when several parameters provide strong directional information. Simulations show substantial power gains for the two-step test over the least favorable and competing procedures. Empirical applications examine unilateral divorce laws and the college-proximity instrument.

translated_abstract: 本文研究检验有限个参数之间符号一致性的问题，其应用包括动态处理效应、工具变量有效性以及劳动力市场歧视。我们提出了能够处理相关估计量的最不利检验和两步检验。这两种检验均有参数与非参数自助法的实现形式，并具有一致渐近有效性。尽管一般而言两种检验互不占优，但局部功效分析表明，当多个参数提供较强的方向性信息时，两步检验可以获得更高的检验功效。模拟结果显示，两步检验相比最不利检验及其他竞争性方法具有显著的功效提升。实证应用部分考察了单方离婚法与大学临近度工具变量。
tldr: 该论文提出了能够处理相关估计量的最不利检验与两步检验方法来检验有限个参数间的符号一致性，两种检验均具有一致渐近有效性，且当多个参数提供强方向性信息时两步检验功效更高。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes least favorable and two-step tests for sign agreement among a finite number of parameters that accommodate correlated estimators, both uniformly asymptotically valid, with the two-step test gaining power when several parameters provide strong directional information.
